chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'My family do not eat the meat of the sheep.' He said, 'And why?' I said, 'They say that it stirs up the black bile, headache, and pains in them.' He said to me, 'O Sa'd!' I said, 'At your service.' He said, 'If Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had known of a thing more prestigious than the sheep, He would have sacrificed it for Ismail (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيل: Ismail (peace be upon him), son of Ibrahim
key_terms.الضَّأْن: Sheep (specifically referring to the sheep sacrificed for Ismail)
key_terms.الْمِرَّةَ السَّوْدَاء: Black bile (a humoral concept in traditional medicine referring to bitterness or acidity)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: At your service / Here I am (a response of readiness and respect)

ai.seo_question: Why is sheep meat considered superior to goat meat in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) refutes the folk belief that lamb meat incites melancholy (*al-murra al-sawda*) by elevating the animal's status through the *Dhabih al-Badr* narrative. He argues that the Divine preference for the ram in the sacrifice of Ismail (peace be upon him) establishes its inherent nobility, serving as a definitive theological proof (*hujjah*) for its culinary and spiritual superiority over goats.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My family are not eating meat of the goat’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why?’ I said, ‘They are saying that it stirs the bitterness with them, and the black bile (acidity), and the headaches, and the pains’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Sa’ad!’ So I said, ‘At your service!’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Had Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Known of a thing more prestigious than the lamb He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Sacrificed it for Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘My family does not like the meat of sheep.’ He (the Imam) then asked, ‘Why do they not like it?’ I replied, ‘They say that it accelerates bitterness, headache and pains.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O Sa‘d.’ I replied, ‘Yes, my Imam.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Had Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, considered anything more revered than sheep He would have presented it instead ( of the ram) as ransom for Tsma‘il, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’”
